questions.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc,$ $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨1,7,-3⟩$, $c=⟨-8,10,-4⟩$, and  $u=⟨6,9,-4⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
questions.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 7 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 10 \\ -4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 9 \\ -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s-8t=6 \\ 7s+10t=9 \\ -3s-4t=-4\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -8 & 6 \\ 7 & 10 & 9 \\ -3 & -4 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -8 & 6 \\ 0 & 66 & -33 \\ -3 & -4 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -8 & 6 \\ 0 & 66 & -33 \\ 0 & -28 & 14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{66}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -8 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & -28 & 14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+28{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -8 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s-8t=6 \\ t=-\frac{1}{2} \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
t=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}s-8t & =6 \\ s-8(-\frac{1}{2}) & =6 \\ s+4 & =6 \\ s & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=2,\,t=-\frac{1}{2},$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=2b-\frac{1}{2}c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=2\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})=-1.$

questions.problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 9 \\ 10\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -8 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 9 \\ 10\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -8 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=3 \\ -4{x}_{1}+9{x}_{2}=-8 \\ -2{x}_{1}+10{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ -4 & 9 & -8 \\ -2 & 10 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ -2 & 10 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 6 & k+6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-6{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & k-18\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k-18.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k-18\,⇒\,k=18.
$$

questions.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc$, $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨-1,2,3⟩$, $c=⟨3,-7,-9⟩$, and  $u=⟨2,-3,-6⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
questions.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7 \\ -9\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-s+3t=2 \\ 2s-7t=-3 \\ 3s-9t=-6\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -7 & -3 \\ 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-s+3t=2 \\ -t=1 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
-t=1\,⟹\,t=-1.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-s+3t & =2 \\ -s+3(-1) & =2 \\ -s & =5 \\ s & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=-5,\,t=-1,$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=-5b-c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=(-5)\cdot (-1)=5.$

Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 7 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -7 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 7 \\ 4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -7 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=8 \\ -3{x}_{1}+7{x}_{2}=-7 \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 8 \\ -3 & 7 & -7 \\ -2 & 4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 \\ -3 & 7 & -7 \\ -2 & 4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 \\ -2 & 4 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & k+8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k+8.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k+8\,⇒\,k=-8.
$$
